angles.drive: You are ready for a challenge before anyone has finished explaining it. Being tested is where you feel most alive, so you rise to the next one rather than ask what it pays. You give your best to whoever dares you first.

You catch ambition instead of growing it alone. You wake up fast to someone else's hunger, so you would rather run beside a driven person than sit with a quiet plan. You catch the pace of whoever is nearest, for better and for worse.

Going all in is your only speed on a shared bet. You would rather match the boldest person at the table than hold back part of the stake, since part feels like half a friendship. You are generous first and careful a long way second.

Losing is the one thing you take personally, even in a game. Being second feels like being nothing, so you would rather fall out over a point than let it go. Remember that you lose a point far more easily than a friend.

Spending for show is how you look like the bigger person. You would sooner spend where the audience is than save where nobody looks, since you have more Fire than places to put it. Remember that you are paying for applause that was already yours.

Switching off is the single skill you never learned. Your Fire outlasts your day, so you keep going instead of letting a rival pass you resting. You are racing people who went home long ago, remember.

You run toward whatever is catching fire, and the running is the point. The contested deal, the live crisis, the dare with witnesses: your blood answers heat the way others answer comfort. In a world of careful people, you are the one already moving, already lit.

Your asks have no ceiling. The cold call to the CEO, the bid above your class, the public promise that forces the miracle: you say the enormous thing out loud, and enough of it lands to fund the reputation. Fortune does seem to favor you. You invoice it accordingly.

Your energy transfers on contact. The flat team meeting catches current when you enter, the tired project finds voltage, the gathering’s pulse syncs upward to yours. People leave your orbit doing things they had filed under someday. The battery, mysteriously, never bills anyone.

The fuse is short, dry, and pre-lit. The wrong word, the cut-off in traffic, the tone in an email: ignition beats deliberation to the scene every time. Afterward you cool fast and repair sincerely. The people nearby, though, have all learned the smell of smoke.

Other people’s wins sit on your skin like sunburn. The peer’s promotion, the friend’s effortless luck, the rival’s applause: each one stings out of proportion, and the sting talks. It comes out as jokes with edges and praise with subtitles. Everyone reads the subtitles.

Pressure in you does not vent. It stores, silently, behind a warm exterior, until the container fails all at once. The blowups arrive without visible warning, sized for the backlog rather than the trigger, and the cleanup involves people who never saw the gauge climbing.
